framing: architectural section, round 1's flip list applied — structure first, repair made physical
hypothesis: Round 1 returned 0 passes in 10: 4 culled as NOISE, 1 object-not-surface, 1 outline, and the 4 that survived the mechanical culls failed the wall questions. The critic's single most useful line: 'Nothing in the set shows a repair.' Round 1's prompt DID name a timber beam, driven pins and rope — and the generator dropped all of it and returned bare masonry. That is the same shape as Stage 1, where naming the orc work produced an object made OF orc work. The lever this round is PHYSICALITY: describe the repair by what it does to the stone around it — a pin spalls its hole, a baulk stands proud and darkens its underside — rather than by naming the material and hoping. Round 1's other flip items are structural and are applied literally.
description: A section of a dungeon wall seen straight on from the front, filling the frame. Big rough grey stone blocks laid in level courses, the courses running right off both side edges mid-block. Each block is uneven quarried stone broken into two or three close values, darker along its lower edge where dust has collected. The mortar beds between them are uneven: tight and thin in places, crumbled wide and dark in others, packed pale in one or two. Several block corners are chipped back so the joint runs into the face. Laid horizontally across three of the courses is a squared timber baulk that stands proud of the stone, dark along its underside where it lifts off the wall, held by two driven iron pins whose heads sit flat and whose holes have cracked the stone around them. Along the top edge only, a narrow band of the wall's upper surface, a clear value step from the face, its lower join broken and irregular rather than ruled straight. Cold grey stone throughout. Heavy, over-built and plain: nothing on it is decorative.
